title: O.T.I.S. Beta v.1
author: verbalbacklash
selftext:
I thought I would share with this group as well. This is my 1st game building in Godot using various AI agents to help me learn. This is kind of a passion fun project to help me learn but I thought I would share it to multiple places and see what people think. Please let me know if you have constructive criticism, like it , dislike it , or just anything really. Just trying to get some more opinions on the concept and what not. I mainly used Codex for this project though I did a 2d prototype 1st to rough out the idea.    
  
Here are the links to OTIS BETA v.1 , thanks to those who gave feedback in discord on the demo.

comments.author: forrestwear
comments.body: this trailer is terrible. the context of whatever the voice is talking about has nothing to do with what is happening on screen. the circus music loop you have going on in the back is annoying. the voice mentions toast around the 50 second mark, but the actual clip showcases it around the 19 second mark. the game doesn't show anything besides picking up a crate. 2/10 at best

replies.author: verbalbacklash
replies.body: Thanks for the input all correct evaluation of the trailer. I would say in defense it's kinda supposed to be that way to mimic an early as seen on tv commercial but it is a fair point I thought about changing the order of voice to match but after watching several times it kinda grew on me. I think the theme of the whole game is going to be kinda jackey slap dash dev considering the source. Either way thanks for the feedback. Dislikes are welcome as much as likes.

comments.author: verbalbacklash
comments.body:
for those following along .

OTIS Station — Development update since Beta .V2

I've been expanding the story payoffs and making the everyday work of running the station feel better.

• More to discover: Fuller ending content, an expanded Humanity route, and additional collectible/achievement payoffs. I'll leave the details for you to find.

• Reworked mazes: Ten introductory mini-maze exercises, more varied hazards, saved attempts and help after repeated failures. The physical maze has new encounters, discovery-tracking wall maps and an authored Root Archive with deeper OTIS/George material.

• A clearer first shift: A starter crate, four voiced tutorial steps, visible target cues and properly timed toast interruptions. Returning players get an optional, skippable OTIS recap.

• Better handling: More precise interactions with shelves, relays, grates and the spacesuit; improved collision; and safer cargo/reward handling. Store or draw the wrench with R / controller Y while carrying other items.

• Cleaner presentation: A smaller HUD, readable playback-linked captions with an off switch, improved highlights, fullscreen/windowed controls and a clear Save & Quit option. Rebinding, basic controller actions and updated control diagrams are included.

• Less audio pile-up: Story reads are protected from routine chatter. Achievement sounds and ending stings get their own space, effects quiet down under speech, and repeated lines are limited.

• Under the hood: Recoverable saves, smoother background autosaves, voice-loading improvements and a much smaller game data pack.

OTIS remains cynical, observant and occasionally helpful. Hints leave room to connect the clues yourself. Dialogue is locally authored; free-form AI chat has been removed.

These changes are in the development playtest. I'm still testing pacing, difficulty and audio balance. Reports of confusing clues, awkward interactions or interrupted story moments help shape the next pass.
